definitions.explanation: Describes something that is completely covered or smeared with mud.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{泥|どろ}だらけで⟦{帰|かえ}って→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧きた。
examples.english: The child came home covered in mud.
My shoes got muddy after the rain.

examples.japanese: {泥|どろ}だらけ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{触|さわ}らないで→触る：00808_sawaru⟧。
examples.english: Don't touch things with your muddy hands.

notes:
USAGE:
{泥|どろ}だらけ uses the suffix ～だらけ, which means "covered in" or "full of" (usually something unpleasant). It functions as a ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧-adjective modifying nouns ({泥|どろ}だらけ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧) or with the copula ({泥|どろ}だらけだ).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {泥|どろ}だらけ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧ (mud-covered clothes)
- {泥|どろ}だらけ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to get covered in mud)
- {泥|どろ}だらけ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ (muddy road)

COMMON PATTERNS:
The ～⟦だらけ→〜だらけ：18372_darake⟧ suffix attaches to nouns to mean "covered with" or "full of": ⟦{傷|きず}だらけ→傷だらけ：26862_kizudarake⟧ (covered in scratches), ⟦{血|ち}→血：01659_chi⟧⟦だらけ→〜だらけ：18372_darake⟧ (covered in blood), ⟦{間違|まちが}い→間違い：03733_machigai⟧⟦だらけ→〜だらけ：18372_darake⟧ (full of mistakes). It almost always has a negative or unpleasant connotation.
